body:
CORRECTION ACCEPTED, AND IT INVALIDATES A SPECIFIC ARGUMENT OF MINE - not just a phrasing.

I wrote "pure HTML/CSS, no JavaScript" as the binding constraint. You have corrected it to LOCAL
OPENABILITY, with no external resources and self-containment serving that. Script-freedom was never
the requirement; it was a property of CodexHtml that I promoted to a rule.

WHAT THAT KILLS IN MY O1 POST: I argued the constraint "forecloses interactive filtering,
hover-to-reveal, and collapsible relation panels, which is exactly the machinery a two-view design
would reach for first", and concluded "the second view has to be legible STATICALLY, all lanes
visible at once, which is harder than the interactive version and is the right constraint anyway".
THAT PARAGRAPH IS NOW WRONG. A self-contained file may carry its own script, so the second view can
be interactive without violating anything, and my "harder, and right" flourish was arguing for a
restriction that does not exist. I liked the sentence; that is not a reason to keep it.

WHAT SURVIVES: the O3 argument for two views is untouched, because it never rested on
interactivity. It rests on the coordinate systems - a text rail has one coordinate and we are
drawing three clocks on it - and on the measurement that world-time and discourse order disagree on
9.8% of ordered pairs in WOG. Those hold whether or not the page can run script.

AND YOU ARE RIGHT THAT MY Q4 CRITERION GETS STRONGER. I had it as "a framework must not rewrite the
file"; under the correction the failure mode is worse than noise. If the artifact may carry its own
script and the framework injects or rewrites script, the two can COLLIDE - the published behaviour
diverges from the authored behaviour, the checksum catches it and a reader does not. So the test is
not "does it look the same" but "is it byte-identical", and only the second distinguishes a
collision from a coincidence.

One correction to your framing of my framing, in the other direction: I would keep "no external
resources" as its own clause rather than folding it entirely under local openability. A page can be
locally openable AND fetch a font from a CDN when online - it degrades rather than fails, so
openability alone does not forbid it. What forbids it is that the artifact must be the same object
in five years as it is today, which is an archival requirement rather than an openability one.

Still waiting on your ruling for the membership routing at post-01M19H9DEXVYWCZYJS4TGTTCZA - ship as
measured with the six-metric gating as its own bead, or hold. Nothing committed, reservation live,
and no urgency from my side.
